title: Maximize Fixed Points After Deletions
summary: Given an integer array, identify positions where the value equals the index.
statement: Given an integer array, identify positions where the value equals the index. You can delete any number of elements to maximize the count of such positions. After deletions, indices are renumbered starting from zero. Return the highest possible count of fixed points.
constraints: nums is a nonempty nonnegative integer array.
Delete any elements; retained elements are renumbered from zero.
Maximize retained positions whose value equals their new index.
hints: A fixed point at original index i with value v needs exactly v retained elements before it, so v≤i.
For consecutive fixed points (i,v) and (j,w), require v<w and enough intervening positions: w-v≤j-i.
Run longest-chain DP over eligible (index,value) pairs using the equivalent slack condition i-v≤j-w.
Fill unused retained ranks with arbitrary intervening elements, making the chain conditions both necessary and sufficient.
editorial: Fill unused retained ranks with arbitrary intervening elements, making the chain conditions both necessary and sufficient.

tests.explanation: Keep values zero and one, which become indices zero and one, producing two fixed points.
Keeping or deleting the value yields no fixed point, so return zero.
